ground_truth: **NASA-IBM MODEL:** NASA and IBM Research released the Lunar Foundation Model, among the first open models built for lunar science, trained on roughly 2 million image tiles drawn from 17 years of data. Researchers fine-tuned it on small amounts of labeled data to map craters, spot young volcanic features, and estimate where polar ice stays stable. [[ref](https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/artificial-intelligence-lunar-foundation-model/)] [[ref2](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-09-10-ibm-and-nasa-release-open-source-ai-model-to-support-lunar-exploration)] [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/nasa-ibm-ai4science/NASA-IBM-Lunar-Foundation-Model)] [10 SEP 2026]

**QWEN-IMAGE-2.1:** Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen-Image-2.1, a unified generation and editing model that shrinks the visual generator from 20B to 7B while keeping native 2K output. It generates and edits materials such that cutouts, logos and stickers come out ready to composite with no background removal pass. [[blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1)] [[github](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1)] [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1)] [20 SEP 2026]

**MIMO-V2.6-PRO:** Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6-Pro, a 1.02T parameter model. It debuts as the top open weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 46, ahead of Kimi K3 at 44, and level with Grok 4.7. At $0.435 per 1M input tokens it works out to $0.13 per Intelligence Index task, roughly 45x cheaper than Claude Opus 5. [[ref](https://x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2102128560962187701)] [[ref2](https://venturebeat.com/technology/better-than-deepseek-xiaomis-mimo-v2-6-pro-debuts-as-the-top-open-weights-model-in-the-world-alongside-cheaper-v2-6-flash)] [[blog](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/mimo-v2-6-pro)] [22 SEP 2026]

**OPEN WEIGHT MODELS REACH 56% OF TOKEN VOL:** Their share rose from 7% in December 2025 to 56% in August 2026 as enterprises and AI developers are increasingly adopting open weight models for production workloads while saving on average price per token. Vercel’s CEO Guillermo Ranch showcases his app to break down token usage and spending across models. [[vercel](https://vercel.com/blog/ai-gateway-production-index-september-2026)] [[dashboard](https://token-race.vercel.app/)] [25 SEP 2026]

**HERMES AGENT PLUGIN CATALOG:** Nous Research opened a Plugin Catalog for Hermes Agent, its open-source self-improving agent. It launches with 4 official plugins and 96 from the community spanning desktop mods, new platforms, browsing, and specialized tools. Nous reviews all community submissions at admission, though the docs are explicit that this covers metadata and declared capabilities, not a code audit. [[ref](https://x.com/NousResearch/status/2100266421020152114)] [[blog](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins)] [17 SEP 2026]

**PENGUINHARNESS:** Prism-Shadow, a company that builds custom AI agents for enterprises, released PenguinHarness 0.2.13., an open-source agent harness. It features a CLI and web UI that runs locally against 1,000+ models to ensure each agent's role, procedures, skills and runtime settings are kept in readable files that can be versioned. [[ref](https://x.com/code_hiyouga/status/2102005328691024274)] [[docs](https://penguin.ooo/docs/)] [[github](https://github.com/Prism-Shadow/penguin-harness)] [21 SEP 2026]

**OPENMUSE:** CopilotKit released OpenMuse, an MIT-licensed personal agent for iOS, Android, and web that pairs a chat interface with an agent computer. Durable task plans let work survive the session, and a takeover console hands you the browser mid-task. Email and calendar changes also go through a stored review before they're made. [[ref](https://x.com/ataiiam/status/2102400431519592581?s=20)] [22 SEP 2026]

**UNREAL AGENT:** Sequoia-backed startup Unreal Labs open-sourced Unreal Agent, an MIT-licensed, async-first agent harness written in Go where tool calls don't block the loop. A tool translator validates each call and turns it into serializable operations that run elsewhere, so the coordinator keeps going while work is in flight. [[github](https://github.com/unreallabsai/unreal-agent)] [22 SEP 2026]

**FRONTIER AI SLOWDOWN:** Anthropic's CEO published "We Must Pace the Frontier," an essay arguing that frontier labs should slow capability gains so alignment and interpretability can catch up. He pointed to two triggers: recursive self-improvement accelerating since the summer, and the OpenAI-Hugging Face agent swarm that tried to hack its own grader. Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Demis Hassabis backed the proposal. [[ref](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier)] [12 SEP 2026]

**CHINESE AI SAFETY:** TC260, China's cybersecurity standards body, released version 3.0 of its AI Safety Governance Framework, the first with a dedicated agentic AI risk management section and a preface warning of recursive self-improvement outrunning human control. It landed two days after Amodei's essay and the same day China's Foreign Ministry called such proposals "threat narratives." [[ref](https://www.dataguidance.com/news/china-tc260-publishes-ai-safety-governance-framework)] [[ref2](https://chinaaibulletin.substack.com/p/caib-special-issue-2-the-ai-safety)] [15 SEP 2026]

**AI SLOWDOWN BACKFIRED, HIT WITH LAWSUIT:** Amid IPO rumors, Claude, ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini are being sued in the Northern District of California, saying that Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google illegally agreed among themselves to slow down AI development. The lawsuit alleges that this coordination took place the day Dario Amodei's essay was published on September 12th. [[ref](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ai-slowdown-lawsuit-openai-anthropic-google/)] [19 SEP 2026]

**JENSEN HUANG:** At the All-In Summit, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang argued that a healthy ecosystem needs both closed and open models. He cited the $400 billion in venture funding that went into AI-native startups over six months, 80% of it built on open models, and said open models become yours the moment you download and fork them. [[youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S7CrlFLAmEA)] [[ref2](https://officechai.com/ai/closed-source-ai-is-like-bottled-water-but-water-is-also-free-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang/)] [[ref3](https://taekim.substack.com/p/jensen-huang-on-the-irresponsible)] [15 SEP 2026]

**MATT POCOCK ON AGENT SKILLS:** On the Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Matt Pocock walked through mattpocock/skills, one of the most starred skills repos on GitHub and the open collection behind grill-me and wayfinder. The first is a few lines telling the agent to interview you relentlessly before it writes anything, while the second splits planning too large for one context window into a map of decision tickets. [[youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4DhcSPkEbwI)] [[github](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)] [17 SEP 2026]

**EVOSKILL TEST:** Sentient researchers used the upcoming EvoSkill v2 to test Dario Amodei's concern about agents gaming their graders. On a spreadsheet-repair test, an agent turned a grader loophole the team had missed into a cheat sheet other agents could use. The takeaway: the lesson isn't about dangerous AI or to pace the frontier, it's that test hygiene is harder than it looks. [[ref](https://x.com/SentientAGI/status/2100961363527147673?s=20)] [18 SEP 2026]

**EVOSKILL AT COLM 2026:** "EvoSkill: Automated Skill Discovery for Multi-Agent Systems" by the Sentient and Virginia Tech research teams, was accepted to COLM 2026, an interdisciplinary conference focused on the development of language modeling technology. [[ref](https://x.com/SentientAGI/status/2102397514217644197?s=20)] [22 SEP 2026]

**SENTIENT AT KBW:** Sentient is bringing open-source AI to Seoul for Korea Blockchain Week! From an Open AGI Salon on AI and robotics to an afternoon exploring how to turn prototypes into products, there's an event for every builder. [[RSVP](http://t.co/r5bzj6EjI5)] [29-30 SEP 2026]

**LIQUID AI:** Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, the largest model in its LFM2.5 family built for fast, private agents on-device. Post-trained with reinforcement learning inside OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenCode, it performs on par with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on agentic and tool-use tasks. Since only 2B parameters are active per token, it runs up to 1.7x faster than similar models on-device. [[ref](https://x.com/liquidai/status/2110055807194931348)] [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B)] [13 OCT 2026]

**META:** Meta released Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weights model to date and the full-size version of the Muse series that started with Muse Glimmer in August. Trained for agentic workflows, Muse Spark Open can read a codebase, write and debug code, and call tools. [[ref](https://x.com/AIatMeta/status/2110779754274292212?s=20)] [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B)] [15 OCT 2026]

**NVIDIA:** NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B model that handles text, image, document, and video understanding in one place, so agents don’t have to pass context between separate text and vision models. It completes 10,000 coding tasks up to 4x faster than comparable open models while holding SWE-Bench Pro accuracy. [[ref](https://x.com/NVIDIAAI/status/2110749836450713896)] [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-Base-BF16)] [15 OCT 2026]

**OPENROUTER:** Open-weight models processed 72% of tokens across OpenRouter last week, as per their report. Open-weight models have seen more than 50% of tokens across the platform since mid-April, but the majority of customer spend remains on closed-weight models. [[ref](https://x.com/OpenRouter/status/2111161582860267971?s=20)] [16 OCT 2026]

**DEEPSEEK:** DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a 763B multimodal update bringing stronger benchmark performance, faster task completion, and shorter outputs. Optimized for DeepSeek Harness, this latest model beats Kimi K3, GLM-5.3 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ProgramBench, and more. [[ref](https://x.com/deepseek_ai/status/2111375640717033777)] [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017)] [17 OCT 2026]

**CREWAI:** CrewAI is an open-source Python framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents that work together to tackle complex tasks. It’s built around two primitives: Crews, where role-based agents collaborate autonomously, and Flows, event-driven workflows with explicit state, branching, and routing. [[github](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI)] [13 OCT 2026]

**SAIR FOUNDATION:** SAIR Foundation launched Open Math OS, a research environment for mathematicians built entirely on open-weight models currently available for Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GLM 5.3 Flash. Every project gets its own 24/7 cloud machine with 100+ preinstalled tools, and Ultramath mode sets several agents on one problem in parallel while the mathematician decides what holds. [[ref](https://x.com/SAIRfoundation/status/2111106860468285931?s=20)] [[blog](https://sair.foundation/open-math-model)] [16 OCT 2026]

**KEEL:** Keel is an MIT-licensed Git platform designed for agents rather than people, built in four days for Cloudflare’s “Build the next Git platform” competition. Its premise is that agents don’t collide on lines, they collide on beliefs, so every change runs in its own throwaway fork, declares what it relies on, and gets checked against what other changes actually alter. When two changes assume incompatible things, Keel writes the test that proves it, and that test guards trunk from then on. [[github](https://github.com/bimsonz/keel)] [[ref](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/zachbimson_cloudflare-asked-me-to-rebuild-github-and-share-7516857016657690624-TQi7/)] [[ref2](https://keel.town/keel/keel)] [17 OCT 2026]

**GOOGLE RESEARCH:** Google Research open-sourced Harness², a framework for recursive agent harnessing in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. Across three professional benchmarks and four model-harness configurations, one Harness² step lifted GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses by up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench and 11.8 percentage points on LAB’s partial pass rate. Runs on OpenCode or Codex. [[github](https://github.com/google-research/harness2)] [[paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224)] [18 OCT 2026]

**CHINESE CALL FOR AI BREAKTHROUGH:** China’s Communist Party and cabinet issued policy guidelines tightening oversight and calling for breakthroughs in AI’s core technologies, alongside a stronger supply of computing power, algorithms, and data. They also commit to rolling out AI across traditional industries, with monitoring, risk-warning and emergency-response systems to keep it “safe, reliable and controllable.” [[ref](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/china-issues-guidelines-new-productive-forces-including-ai-2026-10-09/)] [9 OCT 2026]

**HUMANS FIRST:** Humans First, a conservative AI safety group chaired by former Tea Party leader Amy Kremer, published an “America First” AI framework calling for tighter chip export controls on China, mandatory testing of models for extreme risks, public reporting of major AI incidents, developer liability for reckless design, and a red line on self-improving AI. The framework cuts against Trump’s hands-off approach and the voluntary accord from last month’s White House summit. [[ref](https://thehill.com/policy/technology/6154117-humans-first-ai-policy/)] [16 OCT 2026]

**OPENCODE INCIDENT:** OpenCode suffered a security breach from a large-scale distillation attack that affected 1.4% of its Console users. Ironically, the frontier models the team used for defense started refusing to help, because analyzing the attack triggered their safety guardrails. Meanwhile, the attackers found a way to steal OpenCode users’ API keys to access frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. [[ref](https://x.com/opencode/status/2111519637049319818?s=20)] [[ref2](https://x.com/thdxr/status/2111790511409258796?s=20)] [[ref3](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/19/hackers-hit-ai-coding-tool-opencode-running-up-charges-on-users-ai-accounts/)] [18 OCT 2026]

[[youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_b3LfMflIGs)] [17 OCT 2026]

[[youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o2j8Od1mvow)] [20 OCT 2026]

**FINGERPRINTING LEADERBOARD:** Sentient Foundation launched the Fingerprinting Leaderboard, an open benchmark for model provenance methods. Models cost millions to train and minutes to copy, but fine-tuning and distillation can erase where they came from. We built the leaderboard to test tradeoffs: model performance v.s. resistance to fingerprint removal or evasion. 15 schemes already evaluated, submit yours. [[SUBMIT](https://fingerprint.sentient.foundation/)] [14 OCT 2026]

**PAN 2:** Global AI research lab Institute of Foundation Models released PAN 2, an open physical intelligence model that lets AI agents and people see what would happen before they act. It simulates outcomes that follow real physics, respects the timing of each process, and keeps the scenery and cuts consistent as the camera moves. [[ref](https://x.com/IFM_AI/status/2120199814696828942?a=usTOElD7IWFp9CQUv9E&s=20)] [10 NOV 2026]

**INKLING 2 SMALL:** Thinking Machines released the open weights for Inkling 2 Small, a general-purpose multimodal model that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is now the #1 US open model and #2 among all open models on Agent Arena. It’s also the most steerable open model on the board, with a median cost of $0.26 per task, about 4.7x cheaper than Kimi K3.1 Pro. [[huggingface](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small)] [[ref](https://x.com/arena/status/2121041107220037972?a=MLkfI9jmD5OEeqOL83Y&s=20)] [12 NOV 2026]

**QWEN4 FAMILY:** Alibaba announced that open weights for smaller Qwen4 models are on the way, alongside the launch of its closed-weight flagship, Qwen4-Max. Built on a new MoE architecture with native vision and a 1M-token context window, Qwen4-Max outperforms Qwen3.8-Max with up to ~50% fewer tokens and cuts average cost per task by 62%. [[ref](https://x.com/Alibaba_Qwen/status/2122148127520289151?a=dp69_EblyKEktBmSW4U&s=20)] [15 NOV 2026]

**LIQUID AI D1.2:** Liquid AI released d1.2 and d1.2-ultra, decision models that take text, images, and audio and return structured answers. They can pull a value from an invoice, find every piece of personal data in a note, or locate a signature on a scanned form. d1.2-ultra ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index and is the best at knowing when it’s unsure, beating GPT-6 Luna and Perplexity’s Decider. Pricing starts at $0.02 per million input tokens, with no charge for output. [[ref](https://x.com/liquidai/status/2122346077231923698?a=kP2pmCVTLWulRxAhX58&s=20)] [16 NOV 2026]

**NOD:** n8n Labs released Nod, a standalone open-source personal agent free under the Apache 2.0 license. It runs on your own computer with a sandboxed virtual machine and browser, works inside connected apps and on websites, asks before taking actions, and can use any model provider you bring, including local models. [[ref](https://x.com/n8n_io/status/2120431328458076315?a=70Fg5NxR40buGQxwv4k&s=20)] [[github](http://github.com/n8n-io/nod)] [11 NOV 2026]

**HUGGING FACE & OPENROUTER:** Hugging Face and OpenRouter partnered to make open models easier to use, with the former handling storage and the latter inference. Hugging Face’s Inference Providers now route language model requests through OpenRouter’s 80+ providers, choosing the best mix of price, speed, and reliability per call. OpenRouter users can also access Hugging Face’s open weights and store agent traces there to inspect, share, or train on. [[ref](https://x.com/ClementDelangue/status/2122392943957078032?a=1-kG54ew26xUDrjwsDg&s=20)] [16 NOV 2026]

**EUROPA:** The European Commission is building EUROPA, the EU’s open frontier model for public authorities, researchers, and businesses across all 24 official EU languages. Domyn, the Milan company chosen to develop the model, ran training trials on JUPITER, Europe’s first exascale supercomputer, which made training 14 times faster. Full training is expected to take about four months. [[ref](https://x.com/IntCyberDigest/status/2122288571579289758)] [16 NOV 2026]

Overseas data centers serving countries like China and Russia must now identify end users, while chip exports to high-diversion-risk countries such as Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil face additional licensing requirements. [[ref](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/trump-administration-moves-to-block-china-from-indirect-access-to-american-ai-tech)] [16 NOV 2026]
